There is a word for ‘washing trough’ in the Kremnoan language

by Felicita

Summary

After strange sightings outside of Okhema start to make people uneasy, Phainon takes advantage of a coincidence and convinces Mydei to play along allowing both of them to be taken hostage.
Not only are the kidnappers total idiots unable to tell them both apart – no, Mydei also has to deal with Phainon having a bit too much fun pretending to be the crown prince and angrily cursing in Kremnoan. Or what he thinks is Kremnoan.
Mydei is seriously starting to question his life choices.

Notes

This story is inspired by a conversation I had with a friend a while ago. She was a little amused about my very random knowledge of French words.
I never learnt French (apart from English I took Latin and Spanish at school), but I read a lot, I watch documentaries and movies and I’ve been to France and Switzerland. So I picked up a strange selection of words I would never be able to have any kind of real conversation with.
I transferred that idea to Phainon, assuming he might be frequenting the Kremnoan quarters and that they still speak the language (honestly not completely sure if that is really the case, considering it’s often referred to as ‘old Kremnoan language’ and no-one was ever noted to have any accent or anything like that).
I really tried to imagine in what situations he might have picked them up to, to make it random, but not without any reason behind it. I had fun, I hope you will, too. :D

On a sidenote: I got a few comments about my formatting being hard to read, so I tried to adjust that.
I will be honest, I personally prefer it the other way, but I have no problem using this, if readers prefer it?
Do you like it better? Does this make it easier to read for you? :O

chapters.html:
The cell was far too small for two men their size. They sat accordingly much too close to each other on the only wooden bench in very dim light falling in from the tiny lattice window above.

Since they had been completely stripped of their clothes at arrival both just wore short pants. Their skin was touching uncomfortably warm at the shoulders. It was far too hot in this room anyway.

“Why exactly are we doing this again?” Mydei hissed in a low voice and more than just slightly agitated. Phainon just shrugged with closed eyes.

“For the safety of Okhema’s citizens?” He offered in a whisper.

That was not necessarily the answer Mydei wanted to hear and he grumbled unwillingly.

“Which actually should not be of any concern to you, esteemed crown prince.” His voice was drenched in sarcasm making Phainon finally open his eyes and purse his lips.

“Hey, it’s not my fault these…”

Steps could be heard outside and both fell silent at once. They exchanged one last glance as the door was ripped open and blinding light came in, painting just a dark silhouette in front of them.

And Mydei hoped they would be done with this quickly.

The day had been nothing out of the ordinary. He spent the early morning training with his soldiers, had lunch followed by a short meeting Aglaea had asked everyone to join. A few refugees and citizens had reported some strange sightings of men lingering just outside the city seemingly looking for someone or something.

She asked them to keep their eyes open and considered actually sending someone out to investigate if more incidents should occur. Since so far they had done little more than make people uneasy, it was hard for her to act.

Tribbie and Aglaea soon fell into a discussion about the last meeting of the city treasuries after that and everyone else deemed their own meeting finished.

Phainon stepped up to him.

“Do you want to head over to the sparring grounds?”

A good question, really. They had agreed to meet later anyway, but with little time left until then, they might as well start now. So Mydei nodded.

“Which weapons today?” He asked, adding with a grin: “If you want to keep improving your weaknesses you have plenty of choice.”

That was almost a lie. Phainon was pretty skilled with most weapons they had tried – certainly skilled enough that if he were one of his soldiers Mydei would advise to move on to another. Though, since Phainon’s weapon skills were on equal levels for most choices, the reverse conclusion was that they were equally bad as well and it really would not matter much which one he picked. Therefore his taunt was technically not a real lie.

For a moment Phainon appeared to be sulking, but then a cheeky glint appeared in his eyes. That could mean nothing good.

“You know, I believe I have yet to witness your skills when wielding a Greatsword as well,” he noted sounding almost innocent and curious.

Mydei huffed. “Your point?”

It was true. They never used their actual favourite weapons these days. Probably because it would be pretty obvious who would hold an advantage if they fought with the same weapon type and neither enjoyed unfair fights. (There was just no gratification or satisfaction in an unequal fight.)

Of course they still trained those as well, they could hardly allow to slack off after all, but rarely in sparring with each other, usually going for anything else they could find.

Phainon chuckled softly. „Honestly? I am curious,” he admitted without needing further prodding for once. “And I know what you’re about to say. I’ll pick something else.” His eyes travelled down to Mydei’s hands and he grinned for real now. “If you want me to, I might even try my hand at gauntlets?”

Mydei was about to object and tell him to stop his antics, but… why not? He had fought with a Greatsword before. He had not assumed the same could be said about Phainon and gauntlets, but judging from how he was the one to propose it, he seemed confident enough. Or curious and willing to accept a defeat.

“You really want to get launched into outer space that badly today?” He replied a little gruffly, but he was sure Phainon still saw his amusement. He was (unfortunately) far too good in getting what Mydei did not want to say.

“You make sure to leave the city for that,” Aglaea suddenly cut in with quite a disapproving look on her face. “You both remember that you are banned from using your weapons inside the city’s walls unless there’s an emergency? Switching them won’t change that.” She noted a little dryly. “I don’t want to explain why we need to replace another wall yet again.”

The weight of Phainon’s sword was foreign in his hands. But it was almost more foreign that he could actually feel the cold steel against his skin.

Mydei could not remember the last time he held a weapon in his hand without wearing his gauntlets.

Seeing them on Phainon made the whole situation almost surreal. Phainon had to take off his coat to even be able to put them on. He was currently moving his fingers, testing the flexibility. And he looked quite sceptical if he’d even be able to use them like this.

While the gauntlets held a bit of weight – which he felt missing right now, not surprisingly considering he pretty much wore them all the time – they certainly weren’t heavy enough to cause problems for most people. And for sure not for his rival, who was looking at him almost amused by now.

“You could not have picked something less practical, could you?” He felt the need to comment, but at least changed his stance into something resembling one fit for fighting.

Mydei successfully stopped his lips from twitching upwards. He would like to claim otherwise, but despite the rather ridiculous situation he found himself in, this was by far not the craziest thing they had tried to compete in. In all honesty, it probably didn’t even make the top ten…

He lifted the sword and whirled it at Phainon’s head at once – he was blocked instantly. Mydei had expected that and while he did put some force into the hit, he still held back. And the next few attacks were still rather soft teasing than actual combat.

Phainon was doing better than he had expected him to. Most people would instinctively raise their arms to shield themselves, but trusting that the gauntlets were actually able to securely prevent damage and could be used to counterattack quickly often required a bit of training and exercise.

Either Phainon’s instinct of self-preservation wasn’t very pronounced or he had actually tried something like this before. Knowing him, Mydei suspected a mix of both.

Slowly but steadily their attacks got faster and harder as both of them fell into the well-known rhythm of fighting each other and got more comfortable to take risks.

It was just getting to the good part when Mydei caught movement in the corner of his eye. Somewhere behind him. He used the next opportunity of their exchange of blows to turn sideways and take a look – in fact, someone was watching.

His eyes flickered to Phainon, when he dodged a punch to his waistline. Their eyes met briefly and he knew at once that Phainon had noticed as well.

Two more blows and on the second Phainon reached daringly for the sword to hold it – just shy of cutting himself while doing so. He leaned in as if trying to push him backwards, but there was no real force behind it.

“What are they waiting for?” He whispered, voice very low.

Mydei looked over shortly once more. There were more. At least ten. “For us to finish?”

The question was – finish the fight or exhaust the last of their strength? Not that they ever had fought to that point again – or would for that matter. Especially not outside the city’s walls. But obviously those people were unaware of that.

Phainon frowned, pushing backwards, pulling the sword along and they exchanged another few punches and attacks, before he scampered behind Mydei, rolling over his back and cowering to evade another strike.

“What do we do with them?”

Mydei huffed. Was he seriously asking?

Phainon grumbled lightly, cowered to the side and then punched upwards forcing Mydei to let go with one hand to block the hit against his left flank.

“What if those are the people Aglaea spoke of?”

“So what if they are?” Mydei growled, but still saw the thoughtful look on Phainon’s face for a second. He sighed and rolled his eyes. “What are you suggesting?” He mumbled, still low enough not to be heard by anyone else.

Phainon stayed silent for a moment, before directly reaching for his sword hand and pressing it to the side. “Let’s find out what they want?”

Was he seriously implying for them to pretend to be too tired to continue? He wasn’t right?

Oh, yes, he was. Mydei groaned. That couldn’t be true, why…

The sword fell to the ground, shattering loudly. “You owe me one,” he hissed. “I yield,” he then added in a more normal volume, making Phainon let go and nodding gratefully at him.

“Well fought,“ he replied seconds before several men in dark clothing stormed towards them, pointing weapons. A rather stupid course of action, really. Phainon was still wearing the gauntlets and therefore the weapon he had just been fighting with.

Just how exhausted did these people think they would be after that joke of a fight?

“Hands up! If you don’t fight back, we won’t harm you!”

Mydei looked at Phainon, who answered with almost pleading eyes and he had to fight the urge to roll his own as he lifted his hands.

“What do you want?” Phainon asked.

A spear almost poked him for that. “You will learn that soon enough, crown prince.”

That sentence was nothing new. Honestly Mydei had heard it countless times. What was new, however was that it wasn’t directed at him. They were still talking to Phainon, who looked utterly confused and was about to speak, when three more spearheads almost cut him.

They allowed the men to lead them to a nearby ruin, to undress and disarm them and Mydei was questioning his decision to agree to more each second. Why the hell had he not objected?

Yet he still waited until they were left alone before he voiced the obvious: “Why exactly did we not just lambaste them?” He hissed, crossing his arms.

Phainon sighed softly. “I was hoping they’d bring us to their camp or leader and we could… well figure out what they are trying to achieve?”

“Kidnap me,” Mydei noted dryly. “And we are dealing with real specialists here considering they are unable to tell you and me apart.”

Surprisingly enough Phainon actually rolled his eyes at that. “You know, that part also makes me wonder what in Kephale’s name they think…”

Mydei didn’t speak, but his wicked grin was obvious enough to make Phainon stop.

“Maybe you should at least try to play your role as prince a little better if you want them to keep believing, dear Deliverer,” he mocked.

Phainon frowned. “Are you really suggesting for me to try and impersonate you?” He slowly asked and failed to hide the amused sparkle in his eyes. “I don’t think you actually want to witness that.”

Mydei chuckled. “No,” he agreed. “Even if I’m sure your performance would be quite hilarious. If they have so little clue about me, that will likely expect something different. Don’t be so polite and…” He paused, eying Phainon critically. “In fact, it would probably be more fitting if you spoke Kremnoan.”

Phainon frequented the settlement much more regularly than most would assume, if only because they more often than not ended up training there. It had not been planned in any way, just happened rather quickly. And no matter what else they thought, Kremnoans valued strength and Phainon had proven his in their first duel. Kremnos respected that and so he had been allowed to walk among them with little protest.

Although from what Mydei had heard, Phainon was quite popular with most of his soldiers. Several had already consulted him during their breaks for tips or just approached him for a casual chat. It was not unlikely he might have caught onto a few Kremnoan words during those times.

“Are you able to say anything at all?” He therefore slowly asked.

Phainon laughed softly. “A handful of words, yes. I doubt they’d be helpful though.”

Mydei huffed and leaned back against the uncomfortable wall. “Doesn’t really matter. If they don’t even know what the crown prince looks like, I highly doubt they speak any Kremnoan…”

He would soon come to regret saying that. Or rather not inquiring further. When the kidnappers came back to bring water, Phainon maybe had a little too much fun playing his new role.

As soon as the door opened, he stood, his gaze turning deadly and dark. Even Mydei had never seen that before. And when Phainon spoke, his voice was cold, loud and harsh, the words actual Kremnoan, even if washed out from a heavy accent.

Mydei just wished he had known what exactly would leave his mouth. The tone was perfect, accursing and angry, but…

“Apple pie! Ready, set, go! Good morning!”

It really took all of his willpower and strength to keep his face neutral and not let everyone see that he was stuck somewhere in-between a laughing fit and complete bewilderment.

“Beef broth.” That would certainly be the only time in his life he would ever get to hear this word spoken with that tone. Phainon crossed his arms (only halfway successfully thanks to the chain that still held him to the wall) and snarled: “Holy shit. Sword.”

At least Mydei was convinced now that their kidnappers could not understand a single word he was saying. They flinched from the intensity, put down a jug of water and fled the room. No laughing, no confusion.

Phainon sank back onto the bench, his face back to his normal, much softer expression in seconds. He reached for the jug and took a careful sniff.

“Was that okay?”

Mydei blinked. “Are you aware of what exactly you just said?” He then decided to ask.

Phainon paused. “For about half of it, yes. The rest was just things I heard during training and tried to repeat. Why?”

Mydei brushed a hand over his face. “For my sanity’s sake, let me teach you some sentences to say next time.”

Phainon looked at him in blissful confusion. “For your sanity’s sake?”

Mydei preferred not to answer.

It didn’t take long for another visitor to arrive. In fact, this time several came. They opened the chains and ordered them to follow.

So they walked down the hallway, flanked by several heavily armed soldiers, to a bigger room where two men waited deep in a hushed conversation.

Phainon hissed and acted as if he wanted to get closer, but allowed the guards to stop him with a sword pointed his way. As if he hadn’t been able to easily disarm the man on the spot.

“What’s the meaning of this?” He spit, doing a much better job at pronouncing this time. Mydei noted surprised about himself, that for some reason he actually felt almost joyful at hearing Kremnoan from Phainon. It was nothing he usually would care about and neither had they ever spoken about this, nor had it even crossed his mind. But in a way it felt special, a small and rare…

Whatever it had been, shattered instantly moments later, when Phainon forgot the rest of his text and improvised yet again.

“The soup was really oversalted. Yes, it was! Are you ready?”

Where the hell did he get that from?! And the slurred and blatantly threat-like pronunciation really didn’t help.

Both men turned, fairly unimpressed (noted, they also understand nothing).

“I am sure, the dear prince is able to communicate in a language we will understand,” Idiot One said, stepping a bit closer confidently.

Phainon did not back off, he stood his ground and met his gaze. “What do you want?” He repeated coolly. So coolly that for a moment Mydei actually thought he was seriously angry.

“Just a little negotiation, your majesty.”

If the tone hadn’t been so full of ridicule, Mydei might have considered it a good thing they were assuming Phainon was him. But this was a farce, there would be no negotiation.

Phainon crossed his arms, frowning. “What about?”

A laugh, then, all of a sudden the man sounded serious: “Leave Okhema.”

Admittedly that was not the biggest surprise. Not all inhabitants were happy about their presence, that much was true, but over the last two years a lot had settled down. Okhema had long since been a city full of refugees and the initial worry and dread had made room for peace and routine. The Elders had easier methods to get rid of him, if they really wished to, so who were these people?

If they weren’t Okheman, who else would want them to leave?

He could rule out other Kremnoans, not only would they know what their crown prince looked like, they would also know that this kind of tactic was useless. Kremnoan aristocracy was not protected as it maybe would be in other countries. And last but not least they would certainly not have listened to any of Phainon’s drivel and believed him if they understood anything at all.

“And if we don’t?” Phainon just asked. “Will you kill me?”

A grin on Idiot Two’s face. “First your knight, then you.”

Knight? What knight? He never had… oh. Mydei almost laughed. This kept getting better and better. 

Phainon’s face, however, darkened – probably not out of worry, but honest disdain over talking so easily about ending a life.

“I’m in a good mood,” Idiot One said. “I will allow two quints for you to think about it. Bring them back.”

Phainon shot him a glance that managed to make the guy flinch, right before someone roughly grabbed his arm. He growled and shook him off. “I can walk on my own. Washing trough.”

Washing trough?? Did he think that was an insult?

They were back in their cell, staying silent until they were certain everyone was out of earshot.

“And, how is my impersonation of you?” Phainon joked. Contrary to his facial expression minutes prior he obviously was rather amused than anything else. Mydei was spared having to answer, though, because he kept on talking, more serious now.

“So they want the Kremnoans to leave the city, but they are neither inhabitants nor Kremnoans themselves,” he summed up, mirroring Mydei’s thoughts. “Can you think of anyone who might want to flee to Okhema and would be too scared with Kremnos around?”

Mydei blinked. He had not thought about that. He frowned. “I can’t think of anyone stupid enough to attack us outside the walls, even if they were still thinking of us as enemies.”

“Hm,” Phainon agreed thoughtfully. “Even less if you actually want to be welcomed in. Or maybe they don’t want that either? Do they think of Okhema as defenceless if you’re not around?”

Mydei huffed silently. “Just as foolish of an assumption.”

Phainon chuckled softly and with a hint of irony. “True. But we are talking about people wo assume I am the crown prince and you are my knight. Not sure where they got that from anyway, unless you forgot to tell me I got granted such a title?”

Mydei had tried not to, but his lips twitched now as he shook his head. “Sorry to disappoint you, but there are no knights in Castrum Kremnos. A king who needs protection, isn’t worthy to be king.”

“And here I was thinking you’d surprise me…” Phainon shook his head as well and leaned back against the wall. “Okay, so… let’s head back to Okhema. Before Lady Aglaea or Lady Tribbie actually worry about where we are.”

Mydei nodded in agreement. “We could take their leader with us. The council can then struggle with him and find out their true motives.”

Phainon huffed. “Good idea. Might also keep them busy for a while.”

They mostly kept silent after that, waiting until the two quints were over.

If they had to, they would have been able to get out now, no doubt. But it was probably easier and faster to wait for their kidnappers to get them out of the cell as it would spare them having to break down chains and doors.

Mydei was about to doze off for a bit, when he remembered. “Hey, what was that about the oversalted soup, anyway? Who taught you that?”

Phainon had been daydreaming and startled slightly, looking at him blankly. “Soup?”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “The soup was really oversalted?” He echoed the words.

Phainon just look at him for a moment, then he started laughing. “That means oversalted soup?” He seemed too honestly amused to be playing around. “Oh Kephale… I didn’t know. You remember that day, when you came late for sparring because you had to settle some kind of dispute first? Several people around me said that. I didn’t even cross my mind that they might be talking about lunch.”

What? He would have to look into that some more. Why the hell had the soup been so oversalted that everyone felt the need to comment on it? And who had been in charge of cooking that day?

“Anyway, before I get some more unpleasant surprises – any more sentences you want to get off your chest?” Mydei asked dryly as Phainon was still fighting a laugh.

“In fact, we have covered most of what I know,” Phainon admitted a little softer. “I can say Hello, Goodbye and thank you. Oh, wait and what was it that Telekos used to say? Something along the lines of Don’t think about cutting down trees if you just need sticks?”

It took Mydei a few seconds to understand the words as Phainon spoke them rather inarticulately.

“Ah, something like that, yes…” Where had he dug up this age old saying?

Phainon seemed contemplative, when he looked at him. “Is that something strange? He claimed it meant something like not making a mountain out of a molehill?”

Mydei smiled gently. “It does. But no-one would use that anymore today.”

He shook his head. Maybe she should actually teach Phainon a sentence or two, if only for his own amusement. But not now. Now he just wanted out of here.

They were brought back to the two idiots shortly after.

This time there was no verbal exchange, just eyes meeting and maybe a minute until everyone but the two of them was unconscious on the ground.

Phainon was grumbling because he had not been careful enough and caught a small cut on his thumb from one of the spears pointed at him.

Mydei grinned and was just about to comment on this meaning it was his win, when Phainon looked up. “Shut it.”

So he did know a little more. Mydei left it at that, but couldn’t help his grin when he tossed Idiot One over his shoulder.

About a quint later they stood in front of Aglaea, had endured her sermon about being far too reckless and not setting a good example, and watched some guards drag away the still unconscious idiots.

They went to take a bath afterwards, to wash away the sweat and dirt of that tiny old cell.

Mydei reached for a sponge to scrub his back, when he remembered there was still something he needed to ask.

“Tell me why on Amphoreus you are able to pronounce washing trough of all words perfectly?”

Phainon picked a grape from a nearby plate and flipped it in his mouth, before answering: “That’s what’s making you wonder? Is my pronunciation that bad otherwise?”

Mydei huffed. “Absolutely. I have a hard time understanding what you are trying to say.” He was a little exaggerating. At least partially. He could make a pretty good guess as to which words Phainon actually knew and which ones he had just heard and tried to replicate. He did have a rather strong accent in general, though, proving little more than that he never actually learnt the language. It was not surprising.

Phainon pretended to be hurt and flipped another grape over at him. Mydei caught it wordlessly.

“And here I thought I could try and have a conversation with you.”

Mydei raised an eyebrow in amusement. “With words like washing trough and apple cake?”

Phainon shrugged rather unimpressed. “Hello, washing trough. Thank you. Goodbye.”

A soft laugh escaped Mydei as he continued to rub his skin clean. “Yes. That sounds like a conversation on your level.”

Phainon blinked, then, surprised he laughed as well. “Alright, you win.” He swiped a strand of wet hair out of his face.

“To answer your question: I once got an excellent deal on an authentic ancient washing trough, but I was running out of time to bring it back home. So I took it with me to sparring, placing it out of the way. Of course people noticed and asked me about it. The word was muttered a lot, so I echoed it to ask what it meant. And then they corrected my pronunciation. Supposedly because the way I said it sounded like … what did they say? A derogatory word for people who don’t know how to kiss? At least it made a lot of people laugh.”

Mydei shook his head and allowed himself to sink deeper into the warm water. He should tell his people to stop teaching Phainon nonsense. Or maybe he shouldn’t.

After all it would be a lie to say it did not immensely contribute to his own entertainment.
